page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics processing capabilities alongside balanced compute resources. The instance features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the server bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation, delivering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the server delivers top-tier performance for small to medium language model inference. For a 135M parameter model, it achieves prompt processing speeds of 9944.32 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 464.42 tokens per second. When scaling to a medium 7B model, the instance maintains top-tier performance, processing prompts at 3147.67 tokens per second and generating text at 107.73 tokens per second. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14175.12 and a Passmark CPU score of 14090.9. Memory read bandwidth for large blocks is measured at 88.57 GB/sec, while database operations reach 3658.8 on Passmark.

The fractional GPU allocation offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for projects that require GPU acceleration but do not need a full, dedicated A40 accelerator. This resource density allows users to run GPU-dependent tasks without paying for idle hardware. However, a notable tradeoff is the moderate 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed and the lack of certain advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, which limits its suitability for heavy CPU-only high-performance computing. This server is best suited for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model prototyping, database operations, and general-purpose GPU-accelerated workloads.
